chunks: And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Al-Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Indeed, a bull became wild in Kufa, so the people came out to it with their swords and struck it. They then came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked him about it, so he said: 'It is a valid slaughtering, a living [animal] killed, and its meat is lawful.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (as).
key_terms.الْكُوفَةُ: Kufa, a major city in Iraq.
key_terms.ثَارَ: Became wild, raged, or was stirred up.
key_terms.ثَوْرٌ: A bull or ox, specifically referring to a wild or untamed one in this context.
key_terms.ذَكَاةٌ: Slaughtering, specifically referring to the ritual act of slaughter.
key_terms.وَحِيَّةٌ: A living animal (implying it was alive when struck/killed).

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of a wild animal killed by people with swords considered halal?
ai.summary: This hadith from Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih illustrates Imam Ali’s (as) pragmatic application of the principle of *dhakāh* (slaughter) to wild animals (*al-ṣayd*) killed by humans using weapons, rather than traditional throat-cutting. It establishes the permissibility of consuming game where the animal is killed by the hunter's strike, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the act of killing by a Muslim suffices for lawfulness even without explicit recitation in this specific context of wild beasts.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4166 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Al-Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said: "

A bull in Kufa became wild, and the people attacked it with their swords and struck it. They then came to Commander of the Faithful (as) and asked him about it.
Imam (as) said: 'It is a valid slaughtering, and its meat is lawful.'"
